answer: In PoA, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on the attestation graph, with transition mass damped at each step and anchored in verified identities. A Sybil cluster typically has a sparse external cut, hence low conductance; mixing and min-cut transitivity bounds limit the probability that walks enter it, mathematically capping its aggregate voting weight. Even if summit nodes endorse an ember-linked clique, its influence remains near the nadir unless honest edges increase.
